title: Contradiction from a false-literal chain
statement: Let $c_{\mathrm{idx}}$ be an index, let $\alpha_3$ be an assignment on the extended variable type, and let $m$ map literals over $V$ to literals over that type. For every $j\ge1$ and every list $L$ of at least two literals, if every lifted literal from $L$ is false under $\alpha_3$ and every 3-clause in the chain built from $L$ at counter $j$ is satisfied by $\alpha_3$, then the auxiliary variable indexed by $c_{\mathrm{idx}}$ and $j-1$ cannot be true under $\alpha_3$.
hypotheses_covered: An assignment $\alpha_3$ on the extended variable type
The list $L$ has length at least two
Every lifted literal from $L$ is false under $\alpha_3$
Every chain clause built from $L$ at counter $j$ is satisfied
The auxiliary variable indexed by $c_{\mathrm{idx}}$ and $j-1$ is assumed true in the contradiction implication
replaced:
Fix a clause index $i$ and an assignment $\alpha$ of truth values to the auxiliary
variables. Let $\ell \mapsto \widehat{\ell}$ be a map lifting each literal over the base
variable type to a literal over the auxiliary-variable type, let $j \ge 1$, and let $L$
be a list of at least two literals over the base type such that the lifted literal
$\widehat{\ell}$ evaluates to false under $\alpha$ for every $\ell$ in $L$. If every
3-clause of the chain encoding built from clause index $i$, the lifting $\ell \mapsto
\widehat{\ell}$, the list $L$, and the counter $j$ is satisfied by $\alpha$, then
$\alpha$ cannot also make the entry variable $y_{i,\,j-1}$ true; these hypotheses taken
together are contradictory.
